episodes.title: What is Harm Reduction in Cult Recovery?
episodes.description:
How do you earn the trust of a community that doesn’t trust outsiders? 

You show up for 10 years.

Christine Marie wasn’t FLDS, and she didn’t use religion as a filter for who deserved help. In this clip from At the Brink with Erica Brinker, she explains harm reduction, an approach that began during the AIDS crisis in San Francisco, and how she applies it to women in Short Creek: less trauma, more education and more personal power, wherever a woman is on her journey.

Christine tells Erica why the No. 1 reason women stay in abusive situations is that they have nowhere else to go. That’s why she started Voices for Dignity and the Short Creek Cottage, a charity boutique where women sell their crafts and baked goods and earn money of their own.

She also goes back to the beginning: the 2015 flood that swept away two vans of women and children, the recovery crew where she was the only outsider, and the evictions she and her husband fought as a husband-and-wife team in a patriarchal town. It was that decade of trust that put her in the room when Samuel Bateman arrived.

Christine appears in the Netflix documentary “Trust Me: The False Prophet.”

episodes.title: The Woman Behind Netflix’s Trust Me Survived a Cult First | Dr. Christine Marie | At the Brink
episodes.description:
Warning: This episode includes discussion of child sexual abuse, cult abuse and human trafficking.
Before Netflix’s Trust Me: The False Prophet told how she helped send Samuel Bateman to prison, Dr. Christine Marie survived a cult of her own.
A media psychologist and survivor of cult-based human trafficking, Christine spent years doing humanitarian work with FLDS families in Short Creek on the Utah-Arizona border. When a self-declared prophet began taking young girls as wives, police told her she needed evidence. She and her husband, filmmaker Tolga Katas, kept filming until he confessed on a car ride. She tells Erica Brinker what that moment cost her, why she almost refused to let any documentary be made and what she’d say to anyone in a situation they can’t name yet.
